The salesman made outlandish claims about the product.

cards.def: to do better than someone or something else at a task or activity.
ex: The new phone easily outperforms its competitors in speed.
The fund managed to outperform the market last year.

cards.def: a sudden, strong expression of emotion from many people.
ex: His sudden death caused a huge outpouring of grief.
The news sparked a spontaneous outpouring from fans worldwide.

cards.def: the position, authority, or period of office of the pope.
ex: Many reforms were introduced during his papacy.
In the Middle Ages, the power of the papacy was immense.

cards.def: A low wall along the edge of a roof, bridge, or balcony.
ex: Tourists leaned against the stone parapet to photograph the wide river.
She leaned over the parapet and watched the boats below.

cards.def: A hard, dry Italian cheese often grated over food.
ex: She sprinkled grated parmesan over the steaming bowl of pasta.
The recipe calls for a cup of fresh parmesan cheese.

cards.def: A Christian minister in charge of a parish church.
ex: The village parson visited every family during the long, hard winter.
The parson preached a short sermon about kindness and patience.

cards.def: Something that annoys you.
ex: Loud chewing is my biggest pet peeve at the dinner table.
Slow internet is a common peeve among office workers everywhere.

cards.def: An act you do to show you are sorry for doing something wrong.
ex: He did penance by volunteering at the shelter every weekend.
She cleaned the whole house as a penance for her rudeness.

cards.def: A long, narrow, triangular flag used as a symbol or signal.
ex: The team proudly hung the championship pennant above the locker room.
A small pennant fluttered from the top of the tall mast.

cards.def: Easily annoyed and complaining in a childish way.
ex: He stamped his foot like a petulant child denied candy.
Her petulant outburst surprised everyone in the quiet meeting room.

cards.def: a trained specialist who treats injury and disability with exercise and massage.
ex: The doctor advised her to see a physical therapist weekly.
A licensed physical therapist designed his recovery program carefully.

cards.def: a length of hair divided into three and woven together.
ex: She tied her thick hair into a single long braid.
She likes to wear her hair in a braid at work.

cards.def: Having a large population; with many people living there.
ex: Tokyo is one of the most populous cities in the world.
India is now the most populous country on the whole planet.

cards.def: A sign or warning that something, often bad, is going to happen.
ex: The dark clouds seemed a portent of the coming storm.
Many people read the eclipse as an ominous portent of disaster.

cards.def: A drink believed to have magical or medicinal powers.
ex: The magic potion glowed faintly on the dusty shelf.
The witch brewed a potion in her bubbling cauldron.

cards.def: Relating to the working class of ordinary workers.
ex: The movement claimed to speak for the whole proletarian class.
The pamphlet called for a proletarian revolution against the factory owners.

cards.def: To hit someone or something repeatedly with the fists.
ex: He began to pummel the punching bag with both fists.
The two boxers pummeled each other for several long rounds.

cards.def: Small, weak, and unimpressive.
ex: The team laughed at his puny efforts to lift the box.
The sickly calf looked puny beside the others.

cards.def: A smooth, thick mixture made by blending cooked food.
ex: Stir a spoonful of tomato puree into the simmering sauce.
Blend the cooked carrots into a smooth puree for the baby.

cards.def: A unit for measuring liquid, equal to two pints.
ex: He stopped at the store for a quart of milk.
She filled a glass quart jar with fresh, cold lemonade.

cards.def: A very distant, extremely bright object in space powered by a huge black hole.
ex: Astronomers studied the ancient light from a very distant quasar.
The quasar's enormous energy can outshine an entire galaxy.

cards.def: a colorless radioactive gas that occurs naturally and can be harmful in buildings.
ex: High levels of radon gas were detected in the basement.
Home inspectors often test for radon before a sale closes.

cards.def: a wide bank of earth or a stone wall built to protect a castle or city.
ex: Soldiers stood ready to defend the ramparts against the attack.
Guards patrolled atop the rampart through the night.

cards.def: to repeat the main points of something that has been said or decided.
ex: Let me recap the main points before we end the meeting.
To recap briefly, the project will launch next spring.

cards.def: to be born again in another body after death, according to some beliefs.
ex: Some believe a person can be reincarnated as an animal.
According to the faith, people reincarnate after death into a new life.

cards.def: to break a promise or fail to do what you agreed to do.
ex: He reneged on his promise to help pay for the trip.
She feared he would later renege and leave them stranded.

cards.def: a large bush with bright flowers and leaves that stay green all year.
ex: A huge rhododendron bush bloomed beside the garden gate.
A bank of rhododendrons lined the woodland walk.

cards.def: a large, strong breed of dog often used as a guard dog.
ex: It takes patience to train a rottweiler properly.
They adopted a rottweiler puppy from the shelter.

cards.def: the unit of money used in India, Pakistan, and some other countries.
ex: The Indian rupee fell against the dollar last week.
The snack cost only a few rupees at the stall.

cards.def: a type of hard, spicy sausage, usually eaten in thin slices.
ex: He put a slice of salami on the sandwich.
They served salami and cheese with crackers.

cards.def: a type of bacteria in food that can cause serious food poisoning.
ex: Several diners came down with salmonella poisoning.
The eggs were found to be contaminated with salmonella.

cards.def: to move quickly and smoothly, driven by the wind.
ex: Dark clouds scudded across the sky before the storm.
The small boat scudded before the wind toward the harbor.

cards.def: the clear liquid part of blood, used in medical tests and treatments.
ex: The lab analyzed the patient's blood serum.
Technicians test the serum for signs of infection.

cards.def: to put a sword or knife into its cover.
ex: The warrior sheathed his sword after the battle ended.
He quickly sheathed his weapon when the alarm stopped.

cards.def: to walk toward or away from someone in a quiet, careful way.
ex: A stranger sidled up to us and asked for money.
He sidled away before anyone could speak to him.

cards.def: a mathematical ratio in a right triangle, relating an angle to its opposite side.
ex: The sine of a thirty-degree angle is one half.
The signal forms a smooth sine wave on the screen.

cards.def: dishonest or immoral behavior, especially in politics or business.
ex: The minister faced new allegations of sleaze.
Voters were tired of corruption and sleaze in government.

cards.def: to look around a place secretly to find private information.
ex: He caught someone snooping around his office.
The app was accused of snooping on its users.

cards.def: a short stay in a place, away from home.
ex: After a brief sojourn in Paris, she returned home.
He learned the language during his sojourn abroad.

cards.def: A thin sheet with a design cut out, used to paint the design onto a surface.
ex: She carefully cut a stencil from a sheet of thin cardboard.
The artist painted the letters through a stencil onto the wall.

cards.def: To unfairly treat someone or something as shameful or bad.
ex: Society should not stigmatize sufferers of mental illness.
Many patients feel stigmatized when they admit they need help.

cards.def: A long, narrow strip of colored paper or ribbon used as a decoration.
ex: They hung colorful streamers across the hall for the party.
The children threw paper streamers into the air at midnight.

cards.def: Willing to obey others and accept their control without resisting.
ex: The dog lowered its head into a submissive posture.
He was quiet and submissive to authority all his life.

cards.def: A large amount of a drink swallowed quickly in one gulp.
ex: He took a swig of cold water after the long run.
She paused, then drank a long swig straight from the bottle.

cards.def: A very small amount; a little (used in the phrase 'a tad').
ex: This shirt is a tad too tight across the shoulders.
Add just a tad of salt to balance the sweetness.

cards.def: A lively ballroom dance from Argentina, performed by two people together.
ex: They learned to dance the tango on their honeymoon.
The café filled with the sound of romantic tango music.

cards.def: An expert in science, technology, or management who holds power in government or business.
ex: The new minister is a respected technocrat with years of experience.
For a while the country was ruled by unelected technocrats.

cards.def: The practice of not drinking alcohol.
ex: The temperance movement campaigned against the sale of alcohol.
He practiced temperance and never touched alcohol again.

cards.def: A thin, curling part of a climbing plant that wraps around objects for support.
ex: The vine sent out curling tendrils along the wooden fence.
A thin tendril wraps around the stake for support.

cards.def: A hard, reddish-brown clay used to make pots, tiles, and statues.
ex: Herbs grew in a row of small terracotta pots.
The roof tiles were traditionally made of terracotta.

cards.def: A large, heavy, and usually serious book.
ex: He pulled a weighty tome from the dusty library shelf.
She wrote a massive tome of ancient history.

cards.def: To make someone's hair or something untidy by rubbing or pulling it.
ex: She reached down to tousle the little boy's hair.
The wind gave her a charmingly tousled look.

cards.def: To shock and upset someone so severely that it causes lasting emotional harm.
ex: Witnessing such violence can deeply traumatize a child.
The survivors were deeply traumatized by the earthquake.

cards.def: A frame of crossing strips of wood or metal that supports climbing plants.
ex: Roses climbed up the wooden garden trellis by the gate.
The ivy will climb a trellis if you train it.

cards.def: Small details or facts that are not important.
ex: They chatted about everyday trivia over their morning coffee.
The meeting got bogged down in trivia and achieved nothing.

cards.def: To move slowly and heavily, especially on wheels.
ex: The old bus trundled along the bumpy country road.
The worker trundled a heavy cart across the yard.

cards.def: A man's formal black jacket or suit worn on special evening occasions.
ex: The groom decided to wear a tuxedo for the wedding.
He showed up at the dance in a rented tuxedo.

cards.def: To do less well than you are able to, or than expected.
ex: Some bright children underachieve at school because they are bored.
Students without support often tend to underachieve.

cards.def: To provide too little money for something.
ex: The plan would underfund schools in poorer areas.
The hospital has been chronically underfunded for years.

cards.def: To think that someone or something is less good or important than they really are.
ex: Beginners often underrate the difficulty of learning a language.
He is a badly underrated actor who deserves more praise.

cards.def: An imaginary animal like a white horse with a single horn on its forehead.
ex: The tapestry showed a mythical unicorn in a green forest.
In the story, the princess learns to ride a unicorn.

cards.def: The process or cost of keeping something in good condition.
ex: The family could no longer afford the upkeep of the estate.
The garden needs regular upkeep to stay beautiful.

cards.def: The final result of a situation.
ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new company policy.
The upshot is that we must cut our spending.

cards.def: A person who has recently gained wealth or power and behaves arrogantly.
ex: The veteran manager resented the young upstart in the office.
His rivals dismissed him as an upstart with no real experience.

cards.def: an unexpected and unpredictable change or action
ex: Designers must follow the vagaries of fashion each season.
Outdoor events are subject to the vagaries of the weather.

cards.def: to sell something, especially in small amounts or to the public
ex: Street traders vend goods from carts along the busy avenue.
Only approved sellers are licensed to vend inside the stadium.

cards.def: a person who tries to punish crime personally, without legal authority
ex: A vigilante group began patrolling the neighborhood at night.
Angry residents threatened to take vigilante action against the thieves.

cards.def: a short written description or scene that captures a single moment
ex: The film includes a charming vignette about two old friends.
She painted a vivid vignette of daily life in the port.

cards.def: to say or write cruel and unfair things about someone
ex: The campaign tried to vilify opponents instead of debating ideas.
The coach was unfairly vilified in the press after the loss.

cards.def: a salad dressing made from oil, vinegar, and seasonings
ex: She tossed the greens with a light vinaigrette before serving.
He drizzled vinaigrette over the roasted vegetables and fresh herbs.

cards.def: a type of venomous snake with long, hinged fangs
ex: A venomous viper lay coiled beneath the warm flat rock.
The hiker was bitten by a viper on the rocky trail.

cards.def: a person who observes others' pain or private lives without taking part
ex: Through the camera, viewers become voyeurs of a stranger's daily routine.
He accused the press of being voyeurs of other people's suffering.

cards.def: thin but strong and tough, especially in body
ex: The climber had a wiry build and remarkable grip strength.
He was small but wiry, and surprisingly hard to beat.

cards.def: (historical) a man who owned and farmed a small piece of his own land.
ex: His grandfather was a sturdy yeoman with his own land.
Each yeoman farmer held a few acres near the village.

cards.def: unpleasant to taste, smell, or look at (informal)
ex: The medicine tastes yucky, so the children refuse to take it.
The spilled syrup left a yucky mess all over the counter.

cards.def: an atom or molecule that carries an electric charge because it has gained or lost one or more electrons
ex: Chlorine typically forms a negatively charged ion in solution.
The water filter uses ion exchange to remove minerals.

cards.def: the feeling of not being able to believe that something is true or real
ex: He shook his head in disbelief at the news.
A look of disbelief crossed her face during the speech.

cards.def: to take action in order to prevent something from happening or to stop someone else acting first
ex: The company issued a statement to preempt criticism.
Regulators may move to preempt further damage to investors.

cards.def: a stringed musical instrument like a violin but slightly larger and lower in sound
ex: She learned to play the viola at a young age.
The concert opened with a beautiful viola solo.

cards.def: a common freshwater or sea fish with a flat, deep body, often caught for food
ex: The angler was thrilled to catch a large bream at dawn.
The restaurant serves grilled bream with lemon and fresh herbs.

cards.def: an extra note added at the end of a letter after the signature
ex: She decided to add a postscript to thank him again.
He included a brief postscript about the meeting next week.

cards.def: a letter of an ancient alphabet once used by northern European peoples
ex: The craftsman would carve a rune into each polished stone.
Scholars struggled to read the ancient rune on the monument.

cards.def: a mound of stones built as a landmark or memorial, often on a trail
ex: Hikers often build a cairn to mark the mountain path.
A tall stone cairn marked the summit of the hill.

cards.def: a woman admired as the most beautiful and charming person at an event
ex: In her new gown she was the belle of the ball.
She remained the reigning belle at every party that season.

cards.def: showing a complete lack of courage; shamefully cowardly
ex: His craven behavior during the crisis disappointed the entire team.
The general was blamed for such a craven surrender to the enemy.

cards.def: a long-term loan to a company that pays fixed interest but is not secured by assets
ex: The firm decided to issue a debenture to raise new capital.
Investors bought the convertible debenture hoping to gain company shares.

cards.def: a smaller group that is part of a larger set or group
ex: Only a small subset of customers responded to the survey.
These results form a subset of the complete research data.

cards.def: existing only as an idea or in theory, not as something real
ex: The bank reported the notional amount of its derivatives.
The boundary drawn on the old map is purely notional.

cards.def: a sum of money collected from several people for a shared purpose
ex: Everyone put money in the kitty for the office party.
By the end of the trip, the kitty ran out quickly.

cards.def: to separate grain from the rest of a plant by beating it
ex: Farmers once had to thresh the wheat by hand.
The grain was threshed and stored before the winter.

cards.def: a small worm that attaches to the skin and sucks blood
ex: After the swim, a leech attached to his leg.
The guide showed us how to safely remove the leech.

cards.def: a thick, sweet paste made from sugar, used to cover or decorate cakes
ex: She rolled out the fondant to cover the wedding cake.
They covered the cake with smooth white fondant.

cards.def: an Australian animal like a small kangaroo that hops on its back legs
ex: We spotted a wallaby hopping across the quiet road.
The baby stayed warm inside the wallaby's pouch.

cards.def: a small brown bird known for singing beautifully, especially at night
ex: A nightingale sang sweetly in the garden at dusk.
The song of a nightingale filled the quiet woods.

cards.def: a person or company that rents property or equipment from its owner under a lease
ex: Under the contract, the lessee is responsible for all repairs.
The lease clearly lists the lessee's obligations and payment dates.

cards.def: a thorny shrub or small tree that produces white or pink flowers and small red berries
ex: In May the hawthorn was in full bloom along the lane.
Birds feed on the bright red hawthorn berries all winter.

cards.def: a mathematical value showing the power to which a base number is raised
ex: The teacher explained how to find the natural logarithm of a number.
Students learned to calculate the logarithm using a scientific calculator.

cards.def: a small animal like a mouse with a short tail, living in fields
ex: A field vole darted quickly through the tall grass.
The cat waited quietly, hoping to spot a vole nearby.

cards.def: a flat blade that turns in the wind or water, as on a windmill
ex: The weather vane on the roof turned slowly in the breeze.
Each spinning vane of the windmill caught the strong wind.

cards.def: the way a person behaves, looks, or speaks toward others
ex: The nurse kept a calm demeanor during the busy shift.
Her professional demeanor impressed everyone at the interview.

cards.def: a unit of weight used to measure precious stones such as diamonds
ex: He bought her a one-carat diamond for their anniversary.
The rare gem was said to weigh several carats.

cards.def: a person or company that leases property or equipment to someone else
ex: The lessor and the lessee signed the agreement.
The tenant must pay the lessor each month.

cards.def: to spend more money than you have or more than you planned
ex: They overspent on the kitchen renovation.
The department overspent its budget this year.

cards.def: a sweet paste made from almonds and sugar, used to decorate cakes
ex: The cake had a layer of marzipan on top.
She covered the fruitcake with marzipan.

cards.def: to start or introduce something again, especially a product or service
ex: The company plans to relaunch the product next spring.
The brand was relaunched under a new name.

cards.def: to repair or equip something, especially a ship or room, with new parts or fittings.
ex: The company spent months to refit the old ship for passengers.
They decided to refit the kitchen with modern cabinets and appliances.

cards.def: to provide a country or group with weapons again, or to arm oneself once more.
ex: The government moved quickly to rearm the nation after the war.
Neighboring states grew nervous when the country began to rearm.

cards.def: to greatly reduce the number of people living in an area.
ex: War and famine began to depopulate the entire northern region.
Rural towns can rapidly depopulate when young people move to cities.

cards.def: a chemical that an animal produces to affect the behavior of others of its kind
ex: Some insects release a pheromone to attract a mate.
Ants follow a pheromone signal to find food.

cards.def: fat under the skin that makes it look lumpy, often on the thighs and hips
ex: The cream claims to reduce cellulite on the legs.
Many people have visible cellulite and it is completely normal.
